chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from a number of his companions, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abdullah ibn Suleiman al-Sayrafi, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he presented to us food containing roast meat and other items after it. Then he brought a bowl containing rice, so I ate with him. He said, 'Eat.' I said, 'I have already eaten.' He said, 'Eat, for the love of a man for his brother is considered by his extending himself in eating.' Then he marked a portion for me with his finger in the bowl and said to me, 'You must eat up to that,' after I had already eaten. So I ate it.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of extending oneself in eating according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the Shia concept of *mawaddah* (affection) through the physical act of sharing food, insisting that Abdullah ibn Suleiman eat more rice despite being full. The Imam’s gesture of marking the portion with his finger underscores the sincerity of hospitality, where the host’s desire for the guest’s satisfaction transcends mere politeness. This narrative highlights the practical application of brotherhood in daily interactions, emphasizing that true love is manifested in tangible generosity and the sharing of sustenance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundr, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from a number of our companions, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman Al Sayrafi who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> forwarded some food towards us in which was a roast and some things after it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> came over with a bowl in which was rice. So I ate with him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat’. I said, ‘I have eaten’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat, for the determination of the love of the man for his brother by his extension in his eating’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> marked for me a marking by his<sup>asws</sup> finger in the bowl, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘You should eat (up to) that’, after I had already eaten. So I ate it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from a number of his people from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sulayman al-Sayrafiy who has said the following:

“I once was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and food was brought for us with kabab and other things in it, then a bowl of rice was brought. I ate with him (the Imam). He (the Imam) said, ‘Eat.’ I said, ‘I ate.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Eat because the love of a brother (in belief) is proportionate with how much he eats from his food.’ He (the Imam) then marked with his finger in the bowl and said to me, ‘You must eat that after you have eaten.’ I then ate it.’”
